answer: I can't reliably identify the specific study this question refers to, so I can't give its exact findings. The general pattern in this literature is that parallel DeepWalk (typically Hogwild-style asynchronous SGD on skip-gram, with walks generated in parallel) preserves predictive performance, such as node-classification Micro/Macro-F1, when the graph is large and sparse, so that concurrent updates to embedding vectors rarely conflict, and when the learning rate and number of epochs are kept fixed. Speedup is typically near-linear at low thread counts and then saturates because of memory bandwidth, cache contention, and lock or conflict overhead.
